content.user_title: Create and Package Reusable AI Skills
content.value_statement: Building a skill requires consistent structure, clear triggers, and reliable packaging. This skill provides a practical workflow, starter structure, validation, and ZIP packaging guidance.
actual_capabilities: Guides requirements gathering with concrete usage examples and trigger conditions.
Explains how to organize SKILL.md, scripts, references, and assets.
Creates a starter skill directory with editable example resources.
Validates required SKILL.md frontmatter and common quality issues.
Packages a local skill directory into a ZIP archive.
Provides concise guidance for iterative skill improvement.
limitations: It does not automatically determine a skill's domain requirements.
It does not test whether a generated skill works with every AI tool.
The validator checks basic structure and text rules, not code safety or behavior.
Packaging writes a ZIP archive locally and does not publish it to a marketplace.

use_cases.title: Start a new internal skill
use_cases.description: Create a consistent starter directory and document when the new skill should run.

use_cases.title: Improve team documentation
use_cases.description: Move detailed material into references and keep the main skill workflow focused.

use_cases.title: Prepare a skill for distribution
use_cases.description: Validate frontmatter and package a completed skill into a local ZIP archive.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a skill for reviewing pull requests. Ask for examples, triggers, and the desired workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Plan skill resources
prompt_templates.prompt: I am creating a data-quality skill. Identify which instructions belong in SKILL.md and which resources should be scripts, references, or assets.

prompt_templates.title: Review an existing skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill structure for unclear triggers, duplicated guidance, and unused bundled resources. Recommend specific improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Validate before packaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare my completed skill for distribution. Check its frontmatter, directory structure, resource references, and packaging readiness.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for weekly incident summaries.
output: Suggested trigger conditions for incident-summary requests.
A focused workflow for collecting facts, drafting, and reviewing summaries.
Recommended references for reporting standards and incident taxonomy.

output_examples.input: Review a skill that has a long SKILL.md file.
output: Sections that should move to reference files.
A shorter main workflow with clear resource links.
A checklist for validating metadata before packaging.

best_practices: Use concrete user examples to define triggers before writing the workflow.
Keep SKILL.md focused and place detailed reference material in separate files.
Validate the final directory and remove unused example resources before packaging.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague descriptions that fail to explain when the skill should run.
Do not place large reference documents directly in SKILL.md.
Do not distribute a package with unresolved TODO placeholders or unused examples.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create or improve reusable AI skills with instructions, resources, validation, and local packaging.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: Developers, technical writers, and platform teams who maintain AI skill libraries can use it.

faq.question: Does it create a starter directory?
faq.answer: Yes. The included initializer creates a standard directory with editable example files.

faq.question: What does validation check?
faq.answer: It checks basic directory structure, required SKILL.md frontmatter, TODO placeholders, and several quality warnings.

faq.question: Does packaging publish my skill?
faq.answer: No. Packaging creates a local ZIP archive only.

faq.question: Can it guarantee my skill is safe?
faq.answer: No. The validator does not perform a complete security review of skill instructions or bundled code.
